kurz: Creamy means: thick but smooth, with no lumps and no pools of fat.
bild_im_kopf: Like a freshly mown lawn instead of a ploughed field: lots of small, even particles instead of coarse clods.
bedeutung: Creaminess comes from lots of very small, evenly spread particles: fine fat droplets in an [[emulsion|emulsion]], dissolved starch, or protein that has thickened gently without clumping.
was_passiert: Lumps form when starch [[staerkeverkleisterung|gelatinises]] on the outside before it spreads out, or when protein gets too hot. Pools of fat form when an emulsion splits.
faustregeln: Risotto and pasta: release starch by stirring and tossing.
A stick blender rescues many slightly lumpy sauces.

praxis.text: Risotto turns creamy through stirring, because starch comes off the rice grains.
Cacio e pepe: cheese, pasta water and pepper turn creamy rather than lumpy through tossing.
